# Temple Scroll Column 65 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 65:1 — "fire offerings" vs. "offerings made to the LORD by fire" — אשי

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the fire offerings of the LORD" | Concise, preserves technical term |
| LOGOS | "the fire offerings of the LORD" | Same as EMET |
| PNEUMA | "the offerings made to the LORD by fire" | Expanded for clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS "fire offerings of the LORD." Concise and recognizable; PNEUMA's expansion is unnecessarily wordy.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 65:3 — "cheeks" vs. "jowls" vs. "jawbones" — לחיים

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the two cheeks" | Traditional biblical rendering |
| LOGOS | "the two jowls" | Anatomically precise for meat portions |
| PNEUMA | "both jawbones" | Modern anatomical term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET "the two cheeks." While LOGOS is arguably more precise (the priestly portion was the jaw/jowl area), "cheeks" is the established rendering in English Bible translations and immediately recognizable.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 65:8 — "sale of his patrimony" vs. "sale of family property" vs. "selling family property"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the sale of his patrimony" | "Patrimony" preserves the patrilineal inheritance concept |
| LOGOS | "the sale of family property" | Clear, formal |
| PNEUMA | "selling family property" | Gerund form, accessible |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "the sale of family property." Clear and dignified; EMET's "patrimony" is overly archaic; PNEUMA's gerund is too informal.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 65:11 — "ghost or familiar spirit" vs. "ghosts or spirits" vs. "mediums or spiritists" — אוב וידעני

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a ghost or a familiar spirit" | Traditional rendering of אוב וידעני |
| LOGOS | "ghosts or spirits" | Simplified pair |
| PNEUMA | "mediums or spiritists" | Refers to practitioners rather than entities |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET "ghosts or familiar spirits." The Hebrew refers to the spirits themselves (not the practitioners), and "familiar spirit" is the recognized rendering of ידעני. PNEUMA shifts from entities to people, which is a different interpretation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 65:13 — "whole-hearted" vs. "wholly devoted" vs. "completely faithful" — תמים

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "whole-hearted" | Captures relational completeness |
| LOGOS | "wholly devoted" | Formal, emphasizes dedication |
| PNEUMA | "completely faithful" | Accessible, emphasizes fidelity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET "whole-hearted." The Hebrew תמים in relational context (with עם, "with") means undivided loyalty — "whole-hearted" captures this better than abstract "devoted" or narrow "faithful."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 65:15 — "from your midst, from your brothers" vs. "from among your own people, from your own brothers"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "from your midst, from your brothers" | Literal double prepositional phrase |
| LOGOS | "from among your own people, from your own brothers" | Adds "own" for emphasis |
| PNEUMA | "from among your own people, one of your own brothers" | Rephrases second element |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "from among your own people, from your brothers." The emphasis on "your own" is appropriate for this messianic text but "own" is dropped from the second phrase to avoid redundancy.

**Status:** Resolved with compromise.

---
